correctness.rationale: Linear harmonic forcing satisfies dot w=Bw+v cos(omega t), B stable 2x2. For every real 2x2 B, adj(i omega I-B)=adj(-B)+i omega I. Writing u=adj(-B)v and real symmetric H gives time-average w^T H w=(u^T H u+omega² v^T H v)/(2|det(i omega I-B)|²), since the imaginary cross-term cancels. Positive denominator and affine numerator U+V omega² imply at most one positive root (simple iff UV<0). The supplied example has g′ bounded below by 1-(1/pi²+5/(2pi))>0, equilibrium (1/4,3/4), B=[[-16/3,12],[4/3,-16/3]], v=(4,0), H=[[-1/42,-3/14],[-3/14,33/14]], U=1408/189,V=-8/21; independent exact rational recomputation gives Q=12(9omega²-176)/[7(9omega²+16)(9omega²+784)]. Differentiating yields the unique maximum at omega=(4/3)*sqrt(11+12sqrt(5)), with Qmax=(3-sqrt(5))/896. Analyticity of periodic hyperbolic fixed point and half-period epsilon parity give O_omega(epsilon^4). The nonlinear second-variation H identity is cited as a prior theorem (Zhou arXiv:2610.10602, Thm 5.3), not derived from the adjugate identity itself; its uninspected complete primary source remains a reliance/priority limitation. Zero Q does not fix actual GOE sign.
